page: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with Hyper-Threading enabled. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It has no local storage or GPUs, relying on remote Premium Storage.

Multi-core CPU performance is strong, as evidenced by top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. It also demonstrates strong capabilities in software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, and database operations. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is highly efficient, though single-core performance and text processing benchmarks fall into the average range. Large-scale LLM text generation is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the bottom tier.

Given its high compute density and lower memory allocation, the D64ls_v5 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for parallel processing tasks, software compilation, web serving, and compute-bound database operations. However, it is less suitable for memory-intensive applications or large-scale LLM inference.
